claim: Schistosomes infect hundreds of millions of people in the developing world.
source_text: Schistosomes infect hundreds of millions of people in the developing world.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the epidemiological impact of schistosomiasis, drawing from established public health knowledge.

claim: Transmission of schistosomes relies on a stem cell-driven, clonal expansion of larvae inside a molluscan intermediate host.
source_text: Transmission of these parasites relies on a stem cell-driven, clonal expansion of larvae inside a molluscan intermediate host.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established understanding of schistosome life cycle biology, supported by historical literature and the current study's framework.

claim: The proliferative larval cell population (germinal cells) shares molecular signatures with stem cells from diverse organisms, particularly planarian neoblasts.
source_text: Here, we demonstrate that this proliferative larval cell population (germinal cells) shares some molecular signatures with stem cells from diverse organisms, in particular neoblasts of planarians (free-living relatives of schistosomes).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the RNAseq data comparing sporocyst and planarian neoblast transcriptomes, showing substantial overlap in gene expression.

claim: There are two distinct germinal cell lineages that differ in their proliferation kinetics and expression of a nanos ortholog.
source_text: We identify two distinct germinal cell lineages that differ in their proliferation kinetics and expression of a nanos ortholog.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by FISH experiments showing differential nanos-2 expression and EdU incorporation kinetics between germinal cell populations.

claim: A vasa/PL10 homolog is required for proliferation and maintenance of both germinal cell populations.
source_text: We show that a vasa /PL10 homolog is required for proliferation and maintenance of both populations
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by RNAi experiments showing loss of EdU incorporation and germinal cells following vlg-3 knockdown.

claim: argonaute2 is required only for nanos-negative germinal cells.
source_text: whereas argonaute2 and a fibroblast growth factor receptor-encoding gene are required only for nanos -negative cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing selective loss of nanos-2− cells after ago2-1 knockdown, as demonstrated by FISH.

claim: A fibroblast growth factor receptor-encoding gene is required only for nanos-negative germinal cells.
source_text: whereas argonaute2 and a fibroblast growth factor receptor-encoding gene are required only for nanos -negative cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by RNAi experiments showing reduced EdU incorporation and selective effects on germinal cell populations after fgfrA knockdown.

claim: An ancient stem cell-based developmental program may have enabled the evolution of the complex life cycle of parasitic flatworms.
source_text: Our results suggest that an ancient stem cell-based developmental program may have enabled the evolution of the complex life cycle of parasitic flatworms.
evidence_reasoning: This is an evolutionary inference based on the molecular similarities observed between parasitic and free-living flatworm stem cells.

claim: A population of totipotent stem cells called 'germinal cells' underlies schistosome intramolluscan amplification.
source_text: A population of totipotent stem cells, historically called 'germinal cells', is thought to underlie this unique intramolluscan amplification by undergoing multiple rounds of proliferation and de novo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization
evidence_reasoning: This statement is attributed to historical studies (Olivier and Mao, 1949; Cort et al., 1954; Whitfield and Evans, 1983).

claim: Germinal cells undergo multiple rounds of proliferation and de novo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization.
source_text: A population of totipotent stem cells, historically called 'germinal cells', is thought to underlie this unique intramolluscan amplification by undergoing multiple rounds of proliferation and de novo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization
evidence_reasoning: This is based on historical literature and represents established understanding of schistosome reproduction.

claim: Germinal cells have stem cell-like morphology including high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a large nucleolus, and cytoplasm densely packed with ribosomes.
source_text: Based on previous studies showing that germinal cells in schistosome larvae have a distinct morphology—high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a large nucleolus, and cytoplasm densely packed with ribosomes
evidence_reasoning: This morphological description is attributed to previous work by Pan, 1980.

claim: POPO-1 staining distinguishes RNA-rich germinal cells from other somatic cell types.
source_text: Thus, we screened a number of nucleic acid-binding dyes and determined that POPO-1 clearly distinguishes the RNA-rich germinal cells from the other somatic cell types.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on experimental screening of nucleic acid dyes and observation of differential staining patterns.

claim: POPO-1 strongly stains the nucleolus and cytoplasm of germinal cells.
source_text: In particular, POPO-1 strongly stains the nucleolus and cytoplasm of the germinal cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the staining experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Free-swimming miracidia contain 10-20 germinal cells in the posterior half of the body after hatching from the egg.
source_text: Consistent with previous work (Pan, 1980), we found 10–20 germinal cells in the posterior half of the body of free-swimming miracidia after hatching from the egg
evidence_reasoning: This is based on POPO-1 staining observations in the current study, consistent with previous literature.

claim: In vitro transformation of miracidia into sporocysts triggers germinal cell proliferation.
source_text: In vitro transformation of miracidia into sporocysts triggered germinal cell proliferation
evidence_reasoning: This is observed through mitotic figures in transformed sporocysts and is consistent with previous studies cited.

claim: Germinal cells are observed in mitosis as early as 24 hr post-transformation at a rate of approximately 0.2 mitoses per animal.
source_text: we observed these cells in mitosis as early as 24 hr post-transformation (∼0.2 mitoses per animal)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from microscopy experiments shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The behavior of germinal cells in vitro after transformation is consistent with their behavior in vivo after miracidia penetrate a snail host.
source_text: which is consistent with the behavior of these cells in vivo after miracidia penetrate a snail host (Schutte, 1974).
evidence_reasoning: This comparison is made based on the current in vitro observations and previous in vivo studies.

claim: POPO-1-labeled cells ultimately segregate into a compact cluster in cercariae.
source_text: These POPO-1-labeled cells ultimately segregated into a compact cluster in cercariae (Cheng and Bier, 1972)
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the current study's staining experiments and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: The clustered germinal cells in cercariae are presumably saved for the next stage of development after penetration into mammalian hosts.
source_text: presumably saved for the next stage of development after their penetration into mammalian hosts (Dorsey et al., 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the observation of cell clustering and previous literature on schistosome development.

claim: A morphologically homogeneous presumptive stem cell population persists through the larval stages of the schistosome life cycle.
source_text: These observations reveal a morphologically homogeneous presumptive stem cell population that persists through the larval stages of the schistosome life cycle.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from the POPO-1 staining observations across multiple developmental stages.

claim: The transcriptional profile of sporocysts is enriched for mRNAs associated with germinal cells.
source_text: Since the miracidium-to-sporocyst transition is associated with both an increase in the number of proliferative germinal cells and a switch from a quiescent state to an actively proliferating state, we reasoned that the transcriptional profile of sporocysts would be enriched for mRNAs associated with germinal cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference based on the biological changes occurring during the miracidium-to-sporocyst transition.

claim: Of the 10,852 predicted genes in the annotated S. mansoni genome, 6677 genes were detected in 48 hr sporocysts with an RPKM value above 1.
source_text: Of the 10,852 predicted genes in the annotated S. mansoni genome (Berriman et al., 2009; Protasio et al., 2012), 6677 genes were detected in 48 hr sporocysts with an RPKM (reads per kilobases of transcript per million mapped reads) value above 1
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from the RNAseq analysis presented in the study.

claim: 1662 genes were upregulated in sporocysts relative to miracidia.
source_text: 1662 of these genes were upregulated relative to miracidia
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the comparative RNAseq analysis.

claim: Approximately 30% of genes upregulated in sporocysts (581 genes) share similarity with neoblast-enriched transcripts.
source_text: Indeed, we noticed substantial overlap between these two datasets: of the 1662 genes upregulated in sporocysts, ∼30% of them (581 genes) shared similarity (e-value < e−10) with neoblast-enriched transcripts
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the comparative analysis between sporocyst and planarian neoblast transcriptomes.

claim: More than 20% of neoblast-enriched transcripts (864/4032) share similarity with sporocyst-enriched mRNAs.
source_text: Conversely, more than ∼20% (864/4032) of neoblast-enriched transcripts shared similarity with sporocyst-enriched mRNAs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the reciprocal comparison of transcriptomes.

claim: A total of 4749 1:1 schistosome-to-planarian orthologs were identified using reciprocal BLAST comparisons.
source_text: To better define the similarity between these datasets, we identified a total of 4749 1:1 schistosome-to-planarian orthologs using reciprocal BLAST comparisons (e-value < e−10)
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the bioinformatic analysis of sequence similarity.

claim: 1579 orthologs were enriched in planarian neoblasts.
source_text: 1579 orthologs were enriched in planarian neoblasts
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the analysis of orthologous genes between the two species.

claim: 1525 of the neoblast-enriched orthologs (96.5%) were expressed in sporocysts with RPKM >1.
source_text: quite interestingly, 1525 of them (96.5%) were expressed in sporocysts as well (RPKM in sporocysts >1).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result showing high conservation of neoblast-enriched genes in sporocysts.

claim: 331 orthologs (20% of genes upregulated in sporocysts) are enriched in both neoblasts and sporocysts.
source_text: We examined the overlap between neoblast-enriched transcripts and sporocyst-enriched genes and identified 331 orthologs (20% of 1662 genes that are upregulated in sporocysts)
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the comparative transcriptome analysis.

claim: The 331 overlapping orthologs may contain a core set of genes essential for stem cell proliferation and maintenance.
source_text: This list may contain a core set of genes that are essential for stem cell proliferation and maintenance.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the conservation of these genes across stem cell populations in different flatworm species.

claim: 12% of the remaining schistosome transcripts have orthologs in the planarian neoblast transcriptome.
source_text: As a comparison, 12% (1248/10,125) of the remaining schistosome transcripts have orthologs in the planarian neoblast transcriptome.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result providing a baseline comparison for the enrichment analysis.

claim: The degree of overlap between sporocyst and neoblast transcriptomes likely underestimates the similarity between germinal cells and planarian neoblasts.
source_text: Given the differences in how these datasets were generated (i.e., FACS-purified cells from planarian vs whole schistosome sporocysts), together with the fact that the miracidium-to-sporocyst transformation is expected to result in transcriptional changes independent of germinal cell number, this degree of overlap seems likely to underestimate the similarity between the transcriptomes of germinal cells and planarian neoblasts.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference considering the methodological differences between the two datasets.

claim: Sporocyst-enriched genes include many conserved factors associated with stem cell maintenance and germ cell development in diverse organisms.
source_text: In addition to components of cell cycle and DNA repair machinery, examination of these overlapping gene sets identified many conserved factors associated with stem cell maintenance and germ cell development in diverse organisms
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the identification of specific genes in the RNAseq data and their known functions from the literature.

claim: Sporocyst-enriched genes include a pair of fibroblast growth factor receptors (fgfr).
source_text: including a pair of fibroblast growth factor receptors (fgfr) (Ogawa et al., 2002; Lanner and Rossant, 2010; Wagner et al., 2012; Collins et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This is identified from the RNAseq data and supported by citations showing the role of fgfr in stem cells.

claim: Sporocyst-enriched genes include three components of PRC2 (polycomb repressive complex 2).
source_text: three components of PRC2 (polycomb repressive complex 2; suppressor of Zeste 12, Sm-sz12, enhancer of Zeste, Sm-ezh, and embryonic ectoderm development, Sm-eed)
evidence_reasoning: These genes are identified in the RNAseq data and their roles in stem cells are supported by citations.

claim: 11 out of 37 DEAD-box helicases in the S. mansoni genome are upregulated in sporocysts.
source_text: Strikingly, 11/37 DEAD-box helicases (DBHs) in the S. mansoni genome are upregulated in sporocysts
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the RNAseq analysis.

claim: Three vasa/PL10 homologs are upregulated in sporocysts.
source_text: including three vasa/PL10 homologs (Skinner et al., 2012) that may play a similar role in flatworm parasites to that of vasa in other metazoans
evidence_reasoning: This is based on RNAseq data and inference from the known role of vasa in other organisms.

claim: The conserved germinal cell-enriched genes contain several targets accessible with available small-molecule drugs.
source_text: Interestingly, this set of conserved germinal cell-enriched genes also contains several targets accessible with available small-molecule drugs (e.g., cyclophilin, adenosylhomocysteinase, transketolase) (Crowther et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the identification of specific genes and knowledge of available drug targets from the literature.

claim: Germinal cells could serve as a potential vulnerable point to block schistosome propagation.
source_text: suggesting that these cells could serve as a potential vulnerable point to block schistosome propagation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications based on the findings.

claim: The S. mansoni genome has three argonaute homologs.
source_text: Though piwi and vasa appear to be absent from schistosome genomes (Gomes et al., 2009; Collins et al., 2013), the S. mansoni genome has three argonaute homologs
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome annotation and previous literature.

claim: The S. mansoni genome has two nanos homologs.
source_text: two nanos homologs
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome annotation shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The S. mansoni genome has three vasa/PL10 homologs (vlg).
source_text: and three vasa/PL10 homologs (vlg) (Skinner et al., 2012; Tsai et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome annotation and previous literature.

claim: All argonaute, nanos, and vasa/PL10 homologs except Sm-nanos-1 are expressed abundantly in sporocysts.
source_text: These genes, with the exception of Sm-nanos-1 (Smp_057740), are all expressed abundantly in sporocysts.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the RNAseq expression data.

claim: Sm-ago2-1, Sm-vlg-3, and Sm-nanos-2 are upregulated in sporocysts with different kinetics.
source_text: Among them, Sm-ago2-1, Sm-vlg-3, and Sm-nanos-2, are upregulated in sporocysts, but with different kinetics
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 2C.

claim: ago2-1 expression increases steadily throughout early sporocyst development.
source_text: ago2-1 increases steadily in expression throughout early sporocyst development
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR time course data in Figure 2C.

claim: vlg-3 expression increases sharply following transformation, then plateaus.
source_text: vlg-3 expression increases sharply following transformation, then plateaus
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR time course data in Figure 2C.

claim: nanos-2 mRNA expression does not increase until 4 days post-transformation.
source_text: and nanos-2 mRNA expression does not increase until 4 days post-transformation.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR time course data in Figure 2C.

claim: ago2-1 is expressed in proliferating germinal cells.
source_text: Using this method, we confirmed that ago2-1 is expressed in proliferating germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by FISH showing colocalization with PCNA and EdU incorporation in Figure 3A.

claim: vlg-3 is expressed in proliferating germinal cells.
source_text: vlg-3 is expressed in proliferating germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by FISH showing colocalization with H2A and EdU incorporation in Figure 3B.

claim: 92% of vlg-3+ cells incorporate EdU after a 24 hr pulse (1254 vlg-3+ EdU+/1362 EdU+ cells).
source_text: cells expressing ago2-1 and vlg-3 incorporate EdU after a 24 hr pulse (92% of vlg-3+ cells are EdU+, 1254 vlg-3+ EdU+/1362 EdU+ cells)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the EdU labeling and FISH experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: nanos-2 is expressed in a subset of germinal cells.
source_text: By contrast, nanos-2 is expressed in a subset of germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by FISH experiments in Figure 4 showing nanos-2 expression in only some ago2-1+ cells.

claim: nanos-2+ cells require longer EdU pulses to be labeled compared to nanos-2− cells.
source_text: nanos-2+ cells require longer EdU pulses to be labeled compared to nanos-2− cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by EdU incorporation experiments with different pulse lengths shown in Figure 4A,D.

claim: The ratio between nanos-2− and nanos-2+ germinal cells increases with time after transformation.
source_text: The ratio between nanos-2− and nanos-2+ germinal cells increases with time after transformation.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown quantitatively in Figure 4C based on FISH and cell counting experiments.

claim: vlg-3 RNAi results in loss of both nanos-2+ and nanos-2− germinal cells.
source_text: vlg-3 RNAi results in loss of both nanos-2+ and nanos-2− germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by FISH experiments after RNAi shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ago2-1 RNAi specifically eliminates nanos-2− germinal cells.
source_text: ago2-1 RNAi specifically eliminates nanos-2− germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by FISH experiments after RNAi shown in Figure 5F, where nanos-2+ cells remain but nanos-2− cells are lost.

claim: vlg-3 RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by approximately 90%.
source_text: vlg-3 RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by ∼90%
evidence_reasoning: This is shown quantitatively in Figure 5B comparing EdU+ cell numbers between control and vlg-3 RNAi.

claim: ago2-1 RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by approximately 70%.
source_text: ago2-1 RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by ∼70%
evidence_reasoning: This is shown quantitatively in Figure 5B comparing EdU+ cell numbers between control and ago2-1 RNAi.

claim: fgfrA is expressed in nanos-2− germinal cells.
source_text: fgfrA is expressed in nanos-2− germinal cells
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by FISH experiments showing fgfrA expression pattern relative to nanos-2.

claim: fgfrA RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by approximately 60%.
source_text: fgfrA RNAi reduces EdU incorporation by ∼60%
evidence_reasoning: This is shown quantitatively in Figure 6B comparing EdU+ cell numbers between control and fgfrA RNAi.

claim: fgfrA expression increases during sporocyst development.
source_text: Relative expression levels of fgfrA during sporocyst development with respect to the expression in miracidia, measured by qPCR.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 6A.

claim: Germinal cells in sporocysts and somatic stem cells in adult schistosomes share significant molecular similarities.
source_text: Comparison between sporocyst germinal cells described in this study and somatic stem cells recently identified in adult schistosomes (Collins et al., 2013) reveals significant molecular similarities
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparison of gene expression patterns between the current study and previous work on adult stem cells.

claim: Stem cells may persist throughout the entire schistosome life cycle.
source_text: suggesting that these stem cells may persist throughout the entire schistosome life cycle.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the molecular similarities between larval germinal cells and adult stem cells.

claim: PRC2 components are enriched in planarian neoblasts and are required for neoblast self-renewal and long-term maintenance.
source_text: In planarians, PRC2 components are enriched in neoblasts, and are required for neoblast self-renewal and long-term maintenance (Wagner et al., 2012; Önal et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on planarian neoblasts.

claim: Disruption of ago2 expression in planarians downregulates a specific set of miRNAs and blocks neoblast self-renewal.
source_text: disruption of ago2 expression downregulates a specific set of miRNAs and blocks neoblast self-renewal (Rouhana et al., 2010; Li et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on planarian neoblasts.

claim: Smed-fgfr1 is expressed in a subset of planarian neoblasts.
source_text: Smed-fgfr1 is expressed in a subset of planarian neoblasts
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by implicit reference to previous literature on planarian neoblasts.

claim: vasa is required for the proliferation and expansion of planarian neoblasts.
source_text: and vasa is required for the proliferation and expansion of neoblasts (Rouhana et al., 2010; Wagner et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on planarian neoblasts.

claim: Schistosomes do not have a true vasa ortholog.
source_text: Although schistosomes do not have a true vasa ortholog
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome annotation and previous literature on schistosome genes.

claim: The vasa/PL10 homolog vlg3 may have assumed a 'vasa-like' role in schistosome stem cell maintenance.
source_text: the vasa/PL10 homolog vlg3 may have assumed a 'vasa-like' role in schistosome stem cell maintenance (Tsai et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on functional similarity and is supported by a citation.

claim: vasa/PL10 homologs in monogenean flatworms are essential for germline development.
source_text: Consistent with this idea, vasa/PL10 homologs in monogenean flatworms, which also lack vasa, are essential for germline development (Ohashi et al., 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on monogenean flatworms.

claim: Conservation at cellular and molecular levels suggests an ancient role for these genes in regulating stem cell populations in flatworms.
source_text: This conservation at both the cellular and molecular levels suggests an ancient role for these genes in regulating stem cell populations in flatworms.
evidence_reasoning: This is an evolutionary inference based on the observed conservation across flatworm species.

claim: Neoblast-driven developmental programs inherited from free-living ancestors may have enabled the evolution of complex trematode life cycles.
source_text: In light of these observations, it is plausible to suggest that neoblast-driven developmental programs inherited from their free-living ancestors may have enabled the evolution of complex trematode life cycles.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative evolutionary hypothesis based on the molecular similarities observed.

claim: Pluripotent cells may help worms adapt to obligate parasitism by enabling rapid expansion of infective populations and long-term tissue maintenance.
source_text: These pluripotent cells may help the worms adapt successfully to obligate parasitism, by enabling both rapid expansion of an infective population and long-term tissue maintenance in the hostile environments within their intermediate and definitive hosts.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the adaptive significance of stem cells in parasitic flatworms.

claim: In some trematode species like Echinostoma, proliferating germinal cells exist as two morphologically distinguishable populations.
source_text: Our data revealing the existence of two germinal cell subpopulations (nanos-2+ and nanos-2− cells) are reminiscent of observations in some other trematode species, in particular Echinostoma. In these parasites, proliferating germinal cells are present as two morphologically distinguishable populations (Galaktionov and Dobrovolskij, 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on Echinostoma.

claim: In Echinostoma, one germinal cell population was speculated to be the most 'undifferentiated' cell type, while the other was thought to have more restricted developmental potential.
source_text: One of these populations, smaller in cell size, was speculated to be the most 'undifferentiated' cell type, whereas the other was thought to have more restricted developmental potential and enter embryogenesis directly.
evidence_reasoning: This statement describes speculations from previous literature on Echinostoma.

claim: Morphological heterogeneity in germinal cells was not observed in schistosomes.
source_text: Although this morphological heterogeneity was not observed in schistosomes (Pan, 1980)
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by a citation to previous morphological studies.

claim: The observation that nanos-2+ germinal cells exhibit slower cell-cycle kinetics is consistent with the conserved role of nanos in lengthening the cell cycle in primordial germ cells.
source_text: The observation that germinal cells expressing nanos-2 exhibit slower cell-cycle kinetics is consistent with the conserved role of nanos in lengthening the cell cycle by repressing mitotic transcripts in primordial germ cells from many animals (Juliano et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This connects the experimental observation to known functions of nanos from the literature.

claim: nanos-2 is expressed in germ cells in schistosome adult gonads.
source_text: Along with our observations that nanos-2 is also expressed in germ cells in schistosome adult gonads (Wang and Newmark, unpublished)
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as unpublished data from the authors.

claim: nanos-2 is expressed in adult somatic stem cells.
source_text: as well as adult somatic stem cells (Collins et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: nanos-2+ cells may be more totipotent or germ cell-like, whereas nanos-2− germinal cells may be more primed towards somatic fates.
source_text: it is reasonable to expect the nanos-2+ cells may be more totipotent or germ cell-like, whereas the nanos-2− germinal cells may be more primed towards somatic fates.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the data based on the known roles of nanos and the observed cell behaviors.

claim: Germinal cells are unique in that they are proliferative totipotent stem cells that directly undergo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization.
source_text: Based on the classic literature, the biology of these cells is quite unique: proliferative totipotent stem cells that directly undergo embryogenesis in the absence of fertilization.
evidence_reasoning: This statement summarizes the unique biology of germinal cells based on classic literature.

claim: Despite their unique developmental program, germinal cells possess a molecular signature similar to neoblasts in free-living flatworms and stem cells from diverse organisms.
source_text: We find that, in spite of this unique developmental program, these cells possess a molecular signature similar to that of neoblasts in free-living flatworms, as well as stem cells from diverse organisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion based on the transcriptome comparisons and functional studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: The conserved molecular context of germinal cells may lead to strategies for intervening and blocking disease transmission.
source_text: This conserved molecular context opens access to understanding these cells, and may lead to strategies for intervening and blocking the transmission of the disease.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications of the research findings.
